questions.prompt: The user presses Ctrl+C after the text 'The file has three parts:' arrived and a tool call had started. What does the record keep?
options: Nothing, because the turn was stopped
The text and the tool call, with a made-up result
Only the tool call, because it is the newest block
The text in an assistant/message marked interrupted, without the tool call
questions.explanation: interruptedBlocks keeps text with real content and drops tool calls. The call never ran, and keeping it would need a made-up result.

questions.prompt: Ctrl+C arrives during a retry wait of 8,000 milliseconds. What happens?
options: The sleep ends at once and no retry starts
The wait finishes and the retry runs
The program waits, then stops after the retry
The retry count resets to zero
questions.explanation: The wait listens to the same AbortSignal. When the signal fires, the timer is cleared, sleep returns false and the loop ends the turn as aborted.

questions.prompt: Why does mini-dsh use one AbortSignal for the whole turn?
options: fetch can only accept one signal per program
Every part, from fetch to the retry wait, checks the same signal, so one abort stops all of them
The signal stores the text that already arrived
The provider needs the signal to stop the model
questions.explanation: The signal is passed to fetch and to the wait. One abort() closes the connection and ends any wait, and the loop then writes the end of the turn.
